Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.  That's what I love about learning skills that can create income from home. I'm not looking for another job. I'm building more ways to earn—and more choices for my future. Financial freedom doesn't have to start with something huge. It can start with one product that solves one problem. I went and found five digital products that have each sold over a thousand copies, so you don't have to. They're all on screen so you can go and check the numbers for yourself. Number four is the one nobody expected, including me, so stay for that one. Number one is a brush set at $5 and it's done 23,500 sales. It's not a course, it's not a bundle, it's just brushes. Number two is a travel planner built inside Notion at $20, and that's done over 2,900 sales. There are nearly 20,000 Notion templates on that platform, and it beat all of them because it's about travelling and not about productivity. Number three is a teaching resource at $25 with 2,900 sales, and it was obviously made for teachers by somebody who used to be a teacher — nobody else would have known exactly how to build it that way. Number four is the one I did not expect: a drawing course at $100 with 1,800 sales. A hundred dollars, for foundations in drawing with brushes and charcoal. Nearly 2,000 people have paid for it. That's insane. And number five is a freelance dashboard at $97 with 1,200 sales. Now look at what's in that list. There's no AI in it anywhere. No make money online, no productivity system. It's brushes, travel, teaching, drawing and freelancing — and every one of them is a specific person doing a specific thing. The prices run from $5 all the way up to $100.
